answer: Trust in an agent economy can travel only across a bridge of vouched relationships: each identity earns weight from peers who stake their own standing on it, and a newcomer with no bridge to established agents starts at zero no matter how many keys it mints. Like saffron, trust is scarce because each endorsement costs the endorser real reputation, and a copper-weight audit samples endorsements at random, burning the stake of any cluster caught vouching for its own clones. A farm can mint keys for free, but it cannot mint the bridge.
